name: EuroSAT
description: A novel dataset based on Sentinel-2 satellite images for land use and land cover classification, covering 13 spectral bands and consisting of 10 classes with in total 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced images.
creator: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth
citeAs: Patrick Helber, Benjamin Bischke, Andreas Dengel, Damian Borth. EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification. arXiv:1709.00029v2, 2019.
rai:dataCollection: To construct the image classification dataset, the authors performed two steps: (1) satellite image acquisition by gathering Sentinel-2A satellite images of European cities distributed in over 34 countries, choosing images associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas and selecting images with a low cloud level; and (2) dataset creation by creating 27,000 geo-referenced and labeled image patches of size 64x64 pixels from the obtained satellite images. Images were recorded all over the year to increase variance, and all images were manually checked multiple times.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multi-spectral Sentinel-2A satellite images downloaded via Amazon S3, associated with cities covered in the European Urban Atlas. The source data are openly and freely accessible Sentinel-2 images from the Copernicus Earth observation program.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Sentinel-2A was launched in June 2015, and example images used in the paper span from December 2015 to March 2017; the dataset images were recorded all over the year.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Image patches of 64x64 pixels were extracted from the satellite images to form 10 classes with 2,000 to 3,000 images per class. RGB images were computed by combining bands B04, B03, and B02. For single-band evaluation, the information from one spectral band was used on all three input channels. Bands with lower spatial resolution were upsampled to 10 meters per pixel using cubic-spline interpolation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Satellite images with a low cloud level were selected. The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. The dataset did not receive atmospheric correction, so some images contain color cast and were intentionally retained.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset consists of 27,000 labeled and geo-referenced image patches across 10 land use and land cover classes. The classes were chosen based on visibility at 10 meters per pixel and frequency in the European Urban Atlas. The residential class was created using the urban fabric classes described in the European Urban Atlas. All images were manually checked multiple times and mislabeled images were sorted out to correct the ground truth.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors manually checked all 27,000 images multiple times and corrected the ground truth by sorting out mislabeled images as well as images full of snow or ice. They note that some classes are positively correlated, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes. The confusion matrix shows that the classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Geography: geo-referenced images distributed over European cities in 34 countries.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that the resulting classification system opens a gate towards a number of Earth observation applications, including agriculture, disaster recovery, climate change, urban development, environmental monitoring, land use and land cover change detection, nature protection, sustainable development, deforestation detection, and improving geographical maps such as OpenStreetMap.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset distribution is influenced by the number of represented cities per country in the European Urban Atlas. The authors aimed to cover as many countries as possible and selected images with low cloud level. They note low positive correlation between some classes, especially the two agricultural classes and the residential and industrial building classes.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has not received atmospheric correction, which can result in images with a color cast. The classes were chosen based on being visible at 10 meters per pixel and being frequent enough in the European Urban Atlas to generate thousands of patches. The classifier sometimes confuses agricultural land classes as well as highway and river. A classification system trained with 64x64 image patches does not allow a finely graduated per-pixel segmentation.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is presented as a benchmark and basis for large-scale training of deep neural networks for satellite image classification and land use and land cover classification. The paper provides training and test splits for benchmarking. Proposed real-world applications include land use and land cover change detection and assistance in keeping geographical maps up-to-date.
